sections.h2: Who do I call about property tax in Dallas County, Missouri?
sections.html:
Dallas County property tax runs through two courthouse offices in Buffalo. The Assessor sets the value, and the Collector, Amy Faulkner, bills and takes payment. Both sit in the county administration building at 102 S Cedar Street. The Collector's number is (417) 345-7836 and the mailing address is PO Box 529, Buffalo, MO 65622. Collector hours are Monday through Friday, 8:00 to 12:00 and 1:00 to 4:00, closed on holidays.

The Assessor can be reached at (417) 345-8774 or PO Box 263, Buffalo, MO 65622. The Collector's site gives a clear split of duties. Contact the Assessor about the assessed value of real or personal property, a name or address change, wrong vehicles on a statement or the legal description. Contact the Collector if a statement never arrived or you have general questions about collection.

Other county offices listed by the Missouri Association of Counties include the County Clerk at (417) 345-2632, the Recorder, Stacy Satterfield, at (417) 345-2242, and the Treasurer at (417) 345-2020.

sections.h2: When are Dallas County tax statements mailed and due?
sections.html:
Real estate and personal property statements go out in November. They are due on receipt and become delinquent after December 31. If your statement has not come by the end of November, the Collector asks you to call right away.

  • A mailed payment needs a USPS postmark of December 31 or earlier.
  • Payments postmarked later are returned unprocessed unless penalty and interest are included.
  • Delinquent years must be paid before the office can accept the current year.
  • One check may cover several bills, and the bottom portion of the statement should go in with a mailed payment.

You can pay in person, by mail or online at dallascountymocollector.com, using cash, personal check, money order, cashier's check or a credit or debit card. Cards carry an additional convenience fee. The Collector also warns that the office is not responsible if you pay tax on property that is not yours or miss a parcel you own, so check the legal description on every statement.

sections.h2: How does Dallas County value a house for tax?
sections.html:
Missouri classifies real property into residential, agricultural and commercial groups. Residential is assessed at 19% of market value, agricultural at 12% of production value and other property at 32%, which is how the Cole and Dent County assessor pages describe the classes. Dallas County is a rural county of 541 square miles of land with about 31.6 people per square mile in 2020.

On a $190,300 home, 19% gives an assessed value of about $36,157, to which the local levies for school, county, fire and other districts are applied. Ask the Assessor for the exact districts and levy for your parcel.

sections.h2: How do I contest a Dallas County assessment?
sections.html:
Call the Assessor first and ask for the basis of the value. Under RSMo 137.275, an owner who thinks the assessment is wrong may appeal to the county board of equalization in person, through an attorney or agent, or in writing, and the appeal has to be lodged on or before the second Monday in July. The Dallas County Clerk, at (417) 345-2632, is the office to ask about the hearing schedule.

RSMo 138.060 says the board decides appeals in a summary way and that no presumption exists that the assessor's value is correct. In Dallas County the assessor has the burden of proving the value when the assessed valuation of a property rose at least 15% from the previous assessment, unless the rise comes from new construction or improvements. Take any increase letter with you and compare it to your last notice.

After the board rules, an owner may appeal to the State Tax Commission within the time set in chapter 138 or 30 days after the board's final action, whichever is later, as RSMo 138.430 provides. The Commission corrects assessments it finds unlawful, unfair, improper, arbitrary or capricious. Disputes over exemption or taxable situs instead go to circuit court within 30 days.

sections.h2: What happens at the Dallas County tax certificate sale?
sections.html:
The Collector holds a delinquent tax certificate sale each year on the fourth Monday in August. The 2026 notice set the sale for August 24, 2026 at 10:00 a.m. at the Dallas County Annex Building in Buffalo, and that date has passed. The next sale falls on the fourth Monday in August 2027, which RSMo 140.150 fixes statewide. Delinquent tax, penalty, interest and costs can be paid to the Collector at any time before the property is sold.

  • Bidders must be Missouri residents, or must appoint an agent if they are not.
  • The county warns that some properties could carry hazardous waste, liens or condemned buildings.
  • The redemption period is one year from the date of sale.
  • No interest is paid on any surplus over the tax amount.

State law also requires the Collector to mail notice to the publicly recorded owner before a delinquent parcel is published for sale, first class and then certified if the assessed value is above $1,000. A notice that never reaches you does not remove the tax. If you are behind, keep the mailing address in the tax file current with the Assessor.

sections.h2: What should a seller in Dallas County know about the place and the tax?
sections.html:
Dallas County was organized in 1842 as Niangua County and renamed in 1844 for George M. Dallas, the vice president under James K. Polk. Buffalo is the county seat and largest city, with 3,290 residents in 2020. US 65 links it to Springfield about 28 miles to the south-southwest, and Routes 32 and 73 cross the town. The county belongs to the Springfield metropolitan area. Neighbors are Camden, Laclede, Webster, Greene, Polk and Hickory counties.

The Dallas County R-I district runs Mallory Elementary, Buffalo Prairie Middle School, Buffalo High School and the Dallas County Technical Center. Wikipedia also lists the Hickory County R-I district, with Skyline schools, at Urbana. The county has two cities, Buffalo and Urbana, plus the village of Louisburg and the census-designated place Bennett Springs. The county issued 13 building permits in 2025, and the Census Bureau puts the poverty rate at 17.0%.

When a house sells, ask your title company to request a current statement from the Collector and to settle the tax at closing. If the house changes owners after the November mailing, tell the Collector where to send the new bill.

faqs.q: When are Dallas County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Statements are due on receipt and turn delinquent after December 31. Mail must be postmarked by that date, or the payment is returned unless penalty and interest are included. Call (417) 345-7836 if no statement arrives by the end of November.

faqs.q: Where is the Dallas County Collector's office?
faqs.a: It is in the Dallas County Administration Building, 102 S Cedar Street, Buffalo, MO 65622. Hours are Monday through Friday, 8:00 to 12:00 and 1:00 to 4:00. The mailing address is PO Box 529.

faqs.q: Who sets my assessed value in Dallas County?
faqs.a: The Dallas County Assessor, reachable at (417) 345-8774. The Collector only bills the amount shown on the Assessor's records. Ask the Assessor about value, name changes, vehicles and legal descriptions.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a Dallas County assessment to the board of equalization?
faqs.a: The second Monday in July under RSMo 137.275. Missouri law lets you appeal in person, by an attorney or agent, or in writing. Contact the County Clerk for the hearing date and form.

faqs.q: When is the next Dallas County tax certificate sale?
faqs.a: The 2026 sale was held on August 24, 2026, so the next one falls on the fourth Monday in August 2027. You can pay delinquent tax, penalty, interest and costs before the sale, and the redemption period afterward is one year.
